Sub-Project 1. Appointment and Designation Management System (Enhancement) - (Original Project completed in 2018). A databank and information system of appointments of local treasurers and assistant treasurers made by the Secretary of Finance and designations by the Executive Director of the Bureau of Local Government Finance.

Sub-Project 2. Integrated Information Management System (Enhancement) or i2MSe. The Integrated Information Management System or zi2MSe shall be enhanced and designed with a better and more user-friendly interface, using JavaScript, PHP, and its framework. The enhanced i2MS shall now have two (2) modules, namely: 1. enhanced Documents Management and Archiving System (DMAS), and 2. Enhanced i2MS.

Sub-Project 3. LGU Integrated Financial Tools (LIFT) and the Environment and Natural Resources Data Management Tool (ENRDMT) Systems (Enhancement). The LGU Integrated Financial Tool, or LIFT, was developed in 2015 under a European Union project to enhance and improve the fiscal database systems of the bureau in managing public finances. Implementation of the system contributed to the improvement of data collection at the LGU level and greatly facilitated the sharing of information among the LGU oversight agencies.

Sub-Project 4. Computerization of Certificate of Net Debt Service Ceiling (NDCS) And Borrowing Capacity (BC). In line with the BLGF Quality Policy to improve the effectiveness and quality of internal systems and processes, and to deliver quality service standards in the evaluation, processing, computation, and creation of a web-based application for the issuance of CNDSCBC is necessary.

Sub-Project 5. Data Sharing IT System for BLGF, BIR, and LGU. Under Executive Order 646 of 2007, in order for the LGUs to ascertain, assess, and collect the correct amount of local taxes, fees, or charges, the BIR records pertaining to any person, partnership, corporation, or association subject to local taxes, fees, and charges shall be made available to the local treasurer, his deputy or duly authorized representative. This information System will supplement the database that the LGUs already have, and that would indicate that the incomes declared by business taxpayers to the BIR are consistent with the revenues declared to the treasurer’s office of the LGUs.

Sub-Project 6. Treasury and Assessment Operations Evaluation System. The system will serve as an online platform for evaluating Local Government Units (LGUs), allowing users to generate comprehensive reports that include findings, observations, and recommendations. It will track the status of actions taken based on these evaluations and manage assessment records. The system will also identify LGUs that have not been evaluated over the past three years, ensuring regular and systematic evaluations. Furthermore, it will be capable of updating an e-compendium and a rulings and opinions database, supporting informed decision-making and compliance with applicable standards.

The project is being implemented in four years, starting in Q1 of 2021, and will end on 31 December 2024. On June 25, 2024,  the NEDA Board approved the LGRP's request for 1) a change in scope; 2) a 2-year implementation extension up to December 31, 2026; 3) a change in cost as the GOP counterpart increased due to the finance charges incurred during the extension period; and 4) reallocation of funds. 

There are four components: Output 1: Institutional development and policy support for property valuation strengthened; Output 2: Property Tax Valuation Database and Information Systems implemented; Output 3: Real Property Taxation of Selected LGUs Enhanced; Output 4: Local Assessors Professionalized and Capacity of LGUs Strengthened. For the extension period, the project will focus on the development of the three (3) systems as deliverables under Output 2, such as 1) Real Property Information System; 2) Computer-assisted Mass Appraisal with GIS, and 3) electronic Statement of Receipts and Expenditures/LGU Integrated Financial Tools. On the other hand, some of the spillage activities under Outputs 1, 3, and 4 will still be conducted during the 2-year extension.

In this context, the BLGF spearheaded the creation of the project entitled “Local Finance Capacity Development Project” which has two (2) project phases: Phase I: which aims to expand and upgrade the basic services, facilities, service vehicles and transport, and infrastructure of the fifteen (15) BLGF Regional Offices and one (1) BLGF Central office to strengthen their capacities in providing technical assistance and capacity development mechanisms on more than 1700 local treasury and assessment offices nationwide; and Phase 2 aims to continuously exercise its mandate to be the pioneer in provision of technical assistance and capacity building interventions through the implementation and monitoring of the Standardized Examination and Assessment for Local Treasury Service (SEAL), a three-level certification program to professionalize and provide capacity development for local treasurers. The project aims to (i) strengthen general management and supervision; (ii) expand and improve the basic office buildings and infrastructure, and transportation support and mechanisms, (iii) enhance strategic planning, management information and public information systems and legal services; and (iv) strengthen Local Finance Administration Program and training and capacity development activities, initiatives, and centers for the BLGF Central and Regional Offices, including the social and environmental facilities and services.

The major annual event of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) that officially commences the tax campaign activities. This program serves as the starting point for disseminating vital information to the taxpaying public regarding their obligations, particularly the filing of tax returns and the timely payment of taxes due. Held at the beginning of the tax season, the event underscores the BIR’s commitment to promoting voluntary compliance and fostering a strong partnership between the government and taxpayers. Through this initiative, the BIR aims to increase awareness of tax responsibilities, encourage timely compliance, and highlight the role of taxes in nation-building and improving the lives of Filipinos. The Kick-Off typically features keynote addresses from government officials, presentations on tax policies and digital services, and engagement activities with stakeholders. It sets the tone for the year’s campaign theme and reinforces the message that paying the correct taxes on time is a shared responsibility for national progress.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The BIR is hereby directed to lead, coordinate, and supervise the observance of the Tax Awareness Month and identify the programs, activities, and projects for the celebration thereof per Proclamation No. 486 signed by President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr. on March 1, 2024.

column4: Implementation of an Electronic Invoicing/Receipting Sales Reporting System (EIS) under Republic Act No. 10963
column6: Under the Tax Reform Acceleration and Inclusion (TRAIN Law/Republic Act No. 10963), one of many significant tax administration measures involved the issuance of electronic invoices and sales receipts (e-Invoicing/Receipting) and the submission of electronic sales reports (e-Sales Reporting) to BIR.  The said tax reform measures are expected to simplify taxpayer compliance and improve BIR data analysis.

column4: Budgetary and Treasury Management System (BTMS) Cloud/Subscription-Based Licenses with Software Maintenance and Enhancements
column6: Budget and Treasury Management System (BTMS) Cloud/Subscription-Based Licenses with Software Maintenance and Enhancements, a three (3) year project which is envisaged to be the central core for the Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS).  The BTMS is a centralized database that would facilitate the compilation of crucial data on all parts of government financial operations, from purchase through payment, and every transaction is monitored in real-time by the network.

column4: Cloud Infrastructure Subscription with Support and Maintenance for the Budget and Treasury Management System (BTMS)
column6: Cloud Infrastructure Subscription with Support and Maintenance for the Budget and Treasury Management System (BTMS) is a cloud environment solution for the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) to be used for the BTMS. This solution will be critical in ensuring business continuity of the day-to-day IT operations of the Department and its Bureaus/Services/Offices (BSOs). The BTMS is an integrated, web-based information management system that will replace the existing budget management, execution, accounting, and reporting systems initially used by the DBM and the Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) under the Department of Finance (DOF) for budget execution and accountability.

The Philippines Government Modernization Project is a proposed World Bank–financed Investment Project supporting the Government’s public financial management reform agenda. The Project Development Objective is to improve the efficiency, accountability, and resilience of public resource management. The project focuses on modernizing core PFM functions and digital systems, building on reforms already underway. The Department of Budget and Management leads implementation, with the Commission on Audit as a co-implementing agency, under the oversight of the PFM Committee.
